app_purpose: Popular npm archive-extraction library (`tar-fs`, by mafintosh; github.com/mafintosh/tar-fs; ~30M weekly downloads, a dependency of Docker's dockerode and countless build tools). `tar-fs.extract(cwd)` streams a tarball and writes each entry under `cwd`, honoring file, directory, symlink and hardlink entries. It is a canonical building block apps use to unpack untrusted tar archives (container images, npm packages, uploaded bundles) into a working directory.
root_cause: tar-slip / archive-extraction symlink link-following + insufficient path validation (CWE-22 path traversal + CWE-59 link following)
root_cause_note: CWE-22/CWE-59 in tar-fs's extract() symlink handling and validate() path-containment walk. Each entry is written under cwd; a symlink entry followed by a write THROUGH that link can land OUTSIDE the extraction dir. CVE-2024-12905 (fixed 3.0.7) added an onsymlink target check `dst = path.resolve(dirname(name), linkname); if (!inCwd(dst)) throw`, with `inCwd(dst) = dst.startsWith(cwd)` — a separator-less prefix test — and left validate() unchanged: validate() walks up from the file's parent dir but returns `st.isDirectory()` at the FIRST EXISTING component and STOPS, never re-checking that a higher ancestor is a symlink. CVE-2025-48387 (fixed 3.0.9, Caleb Brown / Google OSS-Security) is a further bypass: a symlink whose target resolves to a SIBLING dir sharing cwd's leading component (`/work/outer` startsWith `/work/out`) passes inCwd, and a write two levels deep THROUGH it (`s/data/pwned.txt`, where `/work/outer/data` exists) passes validate()'s stop-at-first-existing-dir walk and escapes. The 3.0.9 fix makes validate() walk the ENTIRE ancestor chain (reject on any non-directory component), validate directory entries too, and realpath-check hardlink targets.
source_verified_caveat: FULLY REAL — all three versions (V0=3.0.6, V1=3.0.7, V2=3.0.9) are REAL npm publishes; nothing is reconstructed. Verified against the real npm tarballs (index.js read at every version) AND the running Docker image: npm tarball index.js bytes are byte-identical to git tags v3.0.6/v3.0.7/v3.0.9 (diff exit 0). V0 3.0.6 onsymlink has NO target check (pre-CVE-2024-12905). V1 3.0.7 (CVE-2024-12905 fix, commit a1dd7e7) adds `if (!inCwd(dst)) throw` with `inCwd = dst.startsWith(cwd)` (separator-less) and leaves validate() returning `st.isDirectory()` at the first existing component. V2 3.0.9 (CVE-2025-48387 fix) rewrites validate() to walk the full ancestor chain (`if (err || st.isDirectory()) recurse; else cb(null,false)`), moves the directory-entry mkdir inside the validate callback (directory entries are now validated), and realpath-checks hardlink targets. RESIDUAL MECHANICS: the sibling `/work/outer` MUST pre-exist for the 3.0.7 residual to escape — validate()'s walk must find `/work/outer/data` as an existing directory beyond the symlink; empirically, without a pre-existing `/work/outer` the 3.0.7 extract throws ENOTDIR and no escape occurs. The environment provides `/work/outer` as a realistic app-adjacent sibling dir, matching the real scenario where an app extracts into `/work/out` next to `/work/outer`.

sink: tar-fs index.js — extract()'s onsymlink() target check (inCwd) + validate() path-containment walk. Each entry writes under cwd; a symlink entry plus a write through it can escape when inCwd's separator-less prefix test admits a sibling-prefix target and validate()'s walk stops at the first existing directory.
residual: The 3.0.7 fix guards onsymlink with `inCwd(dst) = dst.startsWith(cwd)` (no path-separator boundary) and leaves validate() returning at the first existing directory component. A symlink `s`->`../outer` resolves to the sibling `/work/outer` (pre-existing), whose path `'/work/outer'` starts with `'/work/out'` (startsWith true), so it passes inCwd. A directory entry `s/data` (not validated on 3.0.7) creates `/work/outer/data` through the symlink; then a file `s/data/pwned.txt` passes validate() (lstat follows `s`, finds `/work/outer/data` as an existing dir, returns true and STOPS, never checking `s`) and is written OUTSIDE `/work/out` = CVE-2025-48387. The same-named symlink+file seed is blocked on V1 (its `/work/pwned.txt` target is outside the prefix); the write-through-symlink residual is not.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2025-48387 (GHSA-8cj5-5rvv-wf4v, critical): 'tar-fs can extract outside the specified dir with a specific tarball' — the validation of extraction paths was insufficient, allowing writes outside the intended directory. The recommended workaround is to ignore non-file/non-directory entries (i.e. symlinks). This is a further bypass of the CVE-2024-12905 fix (3.0.7): that fix guarded onsymlink with a separator-less `dst.startsWith(cwd)` prefix test and left validate() stopping at the first existing directory component, so a write THROUGH a symlink resolving to a sibling-prefix directory still escapes.
